title: Assignment 3: Autonomous Robot Navigation in a Multi-Floor Office
description: Compare two complete multi-floor routes using explicit obstacle detours, elevator delays, and destination-floor travel.
assignment_html:
Scenario

Purpose: Write a reusable comparison of two complete multi-floor robot routes.

A delivery robot starts at S = (5, 5) on floor 5 and must reach G = (25, 30) on floor 10. The displayed main route is S -> M1 -> M2 -> E_m. The service route goes straight to E_s plus one half-circle detour.

On floor 5, a temporary construction barrier runs from (8, 5) to (8, 10), so it blocks the straight line from S to E_m. The main route keeps a 0.5 m safety margin by passing below the barrier's lower end through M1 and M2. The robot is treated as a point, so this 0.5 m clearance is measured from the robot's centre. A movable obstacle on the service route adds the detour allowance.

Displayed example inputs

  • robot_speed = 1.0 m/s, on both floors.
  • service_detour_radius = 1.0 m.
  • main_elevator_wait = 30 seconds; service_elevator_wait = 10 seconds. Each wait already includes door opening and boarding time.
  • main_seconds_per_floor = 15 seconds per floor.
  • service_seconds_per_floor = 20 seconds per floor.
  • floors_to_travel = 5 floor intervals, from floor 5 to floor 10.
  • start = (5, 5) m on the origin floor; goal = (25, 30) m on the destination floor.
  • main_elevator = (10, 5) m; service_elevator = (6, 15) m. These locations are the same on both floors.
  • main_waypoints = [(7.5, 4.5), (8.5, 4.5)] m: M1 then M2 on the origin floor.

The supplied calculate_distance helper returns Euclidean distance using math.hypot(dx, dy). route_length(points) adds consecutive straight segments in their listed order. The service route uses a simplified cost model: the direct start-to-service distance plus a fixed detour allowance of math.pi * service_detour_radius, the length of a half-circle arc. Add the full allowance; do not subtract a diameter or invent tangency points. The diagram tells the sequence, not a scaled floor plan.

Note: The allowance pi * service_detour_radius is a deliberately conservative detour allowance, not exact geometry. It is larger than the extra length of a perfect half-circle path, so it also covers the robot slowing down and re-planning its way around the obstacle. Always add the full allowance in this assignment.

Task

Complete evaluate_elevator_routes(...) using its supplied speed, delay, floor, position, and waypoint parameters. Return these eight values in the starter order:

  1. Main entry path through every supplied waypoint.
  2. Service entry path plus the detour allowance pi * service_detour_radius.
  3. Main-elevator-to-goal distance.
  4. Service-elevator-to-goal distance.
  5. Complete main time.
  6. Complete service time.
  7. Exact label Main Elevator or Service Elevator.
  8. The matching smaller complete time.

total time = floor-5 path / speed + wait + floors * seconds per floor + floor-10 path / speed

Rules

  • Use Euclidean distance for straight segments and every supplied main waypoint.
  • Use the function parameters. The grader checks other building layouts and can make either elevator faster.
  • Robot speed is always positive; delays, floor count, and detour radius are zero or more. Coordinates and distances are in meters; times are in seconds. An empty waypoint list means a direct main entry route.
  • Simplifications: the robot is treated as a point (clearances are measured from its centre), and each elevator wait already includes door opening and boarding time. Add no other delays.
  • If the complete times are equal, select Service Elevator as the tie-breaking convention.
  • Return exactly eight values without rounding intermediate calculations.
  • Code runs in a restricted Python sandbox. Use math, common numpy functions (such as np.sin, np.deg2rad, np.array, and np.argmin), and f-strings for printed formatting. str.format, names that start with an underscore (a lone _ is fine), and file or system modules are not available.
  • Do not change the function name, parameters, return order, or exact route labels.
  • Each of the eight equally weighted checks is worth 12.5%; the displayed total uses Python round to the nearest whole percent (ties to even): one correct check is 12%, three are 38%, five are 62%, and seven are 88%. All eight correct checks are 100%.

Before you run the tests

  • Verify that both totals include entry travel, wait, elevator ride, and destination travel.
  • Verify that the route label and best time describe the same route.
learning_objectives: Calculate piecewise Euclidean routes through specified waypoints.
Apply a stated detour-allowance cost model without inventing additional geometry.
Combine horizontal travel, elevator wait, elevator ride, and destination-floor travel into a complete time.
Compare two route alternatives using the same complete cost model.

solution_html:
Floor 5

The main route follows S to M1 to M2 to E_m. The service route is its straight distance plus the stated half-circle detour.

Floor 10

For each option, include the straight distance from that elevator shaft to G.

Complete time

Add floor-5 walking time, elevator wait, five-floor ride time, and floor-10 walking time. The resulting totals are approximately 139.285 seconds through the main elevator and 147.399 seconds through the service elevator, so the Main Elevator is the faster complete route.
